learning_outcomes.text: Provide the student with the basic concepts, equipment, and tools for the design and implementation of industrial automation.
Introduce the student to the structure, programming, and installation of Industrial Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs).
Equip the student with the ability to solve real problems and industrial automation projects.

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Presentation of the course contents.
New functions and elements of industrial automation. Industry 4.0.
Internal Architecture and Configuration of a Programmable Logic Controller
Characteristics of the programmable logic controller.
Configuration of the programmable logic controller.
Practice 1: Description and configuration of an industrial automation system. CPU memory, data types and addressing.
Operating Cycle of a Programmable Logic Controller and Real-Time Control
Practice 2: Introduction to TIA PORTAL software and programming languages. Logical operations.
Electrical, mechanical, operational, dynamic and environmental characteristics.
IEC 1131-3 standardized system for programmable logic controller programming.
Practice 4: Timing, counter and comparison operations.
Control Systems Implemented with Programmable Logic Controllers
Implementation of GRAFCET on programmable logic controllers.
Practice 5: Control systems implemented with programmable logic controllers: Practical case 1.
Practice 6: Control systems implemented with programmable logic controllers: Practical case 2.
Hierarchy, operating modes and safety. Structured design.
Selection of the type of user program structure.
Practice 7: Control systems implemented with programmable logic controllers: Practical case 3.
Practice 9: Programming a PID control loop (I).
Practice 10: Programming a PID control loop (II).

assessment_methods.method: Final theoretical/practical exam and/or cumulative/eliminatory partial exams
Utilization of practical activities (in class, laboratory, computer room, field, visits, etc.)
Resolution and submission of activities (cases, problems, reports, assignments, projects, etc.), individually and/or in groups

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, the final grade (CF) is calculated as: CF = (0.5 * AE1) + (0.3 * AE2) + (0.2 * AE3). A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for the final exam (AE1) and for the practice evaluation (AE2) to pass. If these minimums are not met, but the calculated total score exceeds 5, the final grade will be 4. AE1 and AE2 are recoverable, while AE3 is not. For global assessment, students must take a written final exam, worth 70% of the final grade, and a practice exam, worth 30% of the final grade. A minimum score of 5 out of 10 is required for both the written final exam and the practice exam to pass.
